title: lane H's tests as an ordinary user
note: basis 'shown' means shown in the card's container, by an ordinary account (uid 1000) with its own clone and virtualenv, run with umask 002 and with umask 022, and as root; the bench host was not run (the walk's next run is the proof).

findings.claim: run as an ordinary user with umask 002, the 10K-4, H-89 and H-97 rotate-kek fixtures built their stand-in trees writable by the group, and the product's unchanged checks rightly refused them (10K-4 43, H-89 10, H-97 3, the walk's counts); the fixtures now close the trees they build (tests/host_modes.py), with no assertion changed

test_doctor_fails_a_runner_that_never_ran (4 parameters) asked the machine's own systemd; on a box with trialbox-ops.timer enabled doctor rightly gives the enabled hint, not 'enable --now'; the test now gives doctor a host whose systemd cannot be asked

make test makes /var/tmp/trialbox-<uid>, TB_TEST_ROOT and its tmp/ with the runner's umask (0775 under umask 002); the product's checks that walk the real folders from / then refuse every tree under them (backup_key_ceremony 59, kek_passphrase_review_h96 17, kek_passphrase_file_h96 22, rotate_exposed_passphrase_h97 15, rotate_kek_safety_h97 9, poc_stops_review_h94 3, restic_password 1, runbook_install_commands 1, seal_keys_order 1); tools/pglocal.py mark_test_root now makes the folders it creates 0700 and closes the test root and the folders up to the per-user scratch root it owns (an earlier run's 0775 root included), and the Makefile makes TMPDIR 0700

the box fixture of test_host_commands_own_environment writes deploy/.env with the umask, and the launcher rightly refuses a box file that group or others can write (that file 39, backup_schedule_timer 1, restore_from_the_host_h100 1 under umask 002); #1455's chmod 0o600 there clears all three on master

tools/engine_probe.py writes --out with the caller's umask; the runbook's step runs it under sudo (umask at least 022), but a run without sudo under umask 002 gives a file the rehearsal install refuses ('chmod go-w'), with the fix named in the refusal; the review's 1462-7 says the same

the review's 1462-1: tools.full_set (rc1 line 1) put the test root under --out, which with the clone above it carries the runner's umask, so the walk's run would refuse the ceremony and passphrase trees again; the test root now lies under the per-user scratch root, one per --out
the review's 1462-2: mark_test_root checked exists() then mkdir(), so two runs starting at once on a fresh host stopped with FileExistsError; a folder another run made a moment ago is now no error

the review's 1462-3: a scratch root another account made first was used silently, and its owner could swap the test root; a folder in the chain that another account owns (not root, not sticky) is now refused
the review's 1462-4: a group's setgid folder lost group write, and TB_SCRATCH=/ closed every folder up to /; setgid now counts as shared and nothing is climbed for / or a top-level scratch root
the review's 1462-5: a scratch root named through a link was never closed; it is now compared as a real path
the review's 1462-6: _close_to_others looked with lstat and changed with a chmod that follows links; it now opens the folder once without following a link and uses fstat and fchmod
the review's 1462-8: two more doctor checks in test_ops_runner_on asked the machine's own systemd; the file's _check now gives every check a host of its own

the review's 1462-9: test-pure and ci still make the test root with a plain mkdir -p, 0775 and unmarked under umask 002; nothing fails from it (ci runs make test next, test-pure's tests use pytest's own base folder)

the re-review's 1462-10: a sticky scratch root another account made first was still accepted, and its owner may rename what is in it; another account's folder in the chain is now refused whatever its sticky bit (root's stays allowed)

the re-review's 1462-11: the marker was written through a link, so a root swapped after the checks marked the folder it pointed to; it is now written through the root's own descriptor, opened without following a link
the re-review's 1462-12: two counts named no file list; the exact lists (policy-tests.txt, card-tests.txt, proof-tests.txt) are now beside the page
